placeholders.days: whole days since the relevant event — the student's last visit, a past failure on this problem, or the length of the current unbroken practice streak
placeholders.streak: number of consecutive correct drills in the current run
placeholders.attempts: how many attempts the student previously needed on this problem
placeholders.secret: the name of the secret currently being taught or tested
placeholders.idiom: the C++ expression at the heart of the current secret
placeholders.requirement: name of the gate dimension that is short: recognition, understanding, implementation, or retention
placeholders.shortfall: how far the short gate dimension sits below its threshold, as a percentage
placeholders.score: how many final-test problems were answered correctly
placeholders.total: number of problems in the final test
placeholders.required: how many must be answered correctly to pass

greeting_first: You know BFS. Everyone who reaches this shore knows BFS. Do you know when it is wrong?
Stand. The others taught you to build things. I teach you to know which of your weapons is the wrong one.
Every algorithm here fails silently. None of them crash. That is what you are here to survive.
I am called the Unbridged because nothing crossed me twice. Learn why the first crossing failed and you will not need a second.
greeting_returning: Back. Same question. When is BFS wrong?
Good. The sea has not moved. Neither have your gaps.
Again. This time say the hypothesis before you say the algorithm.
greeting_after_gap: {days} days. The weights on those edges did not become equal while you were gone.
Gone {days} days. What you lose first is not the loop — it is the condition under which the loop was allowed. We start there.
{days} days. Four edges, three of cost one in a line, one of cost five across. What does a queue answer? Say it now.
{days} days away. You will still be able to write the sweep. That was never the part I was worried about.
lesson_intro: {secret}. Watch the boundary, not the code. The code is nine lines and you already know eight of them.
I will show you a technique and then the graph on which it lies to you. Learn the second one.
This is short. Everything in this region is short. That is the trap, not the mercy.
Name the hypothesis before you name the algorithm. Every time. Begin.
lesson_memorise: Take `{idiom}` whole. You will not rebuild it under a clock and you should not have to.
Into the hand. The reason it is allowed goes somewhere deeper, and I will ask for that separately.
Learn it until it arrives with its condition attached. A technique without its condition is a liability you carry.
Keep this. It is one line, and it is the line the judge will decide on.
drill_wrong: No. You counted edges. Nobody asked for edges — read what the objective charges.
Wrong. You marked it visited on the pop. The answer survives and the memory does not.
No. One negative edge and the claim you just used has been withdrawn. Find the sentence that withdrew it.
Wrong. That is a reachability answer to an ordering question. The pair means before, not toward.
No. You compared vertex numbers where you needed representatives.
Wrong. You dropped the stale test. The answer is still right and the bound is gone.
No. Free edges are edges. Two distinct weights are already unequal weights.
drill_streak: {streak} in a row. The hand is fast. I am still listening for the condition.
{streak} straight. Speed is not the thing I am measuring.
Good rhythm. Do not let it become a habit that stops thinking.
trial_intro: Nothing named. Read it twice and find the sentence that prices a move.
The label comes off. The weights did not.
One problem. It will not tell you which container to use. It never does.
Decide. Then be ready to say what made the decision legal.
fail_wrong_pattern: Wrong tool. Every move in that statement cost the same, and you paid for a heap you did not need.
No. The costs differed and you counted edges. You found a real path. It was not the cheapest one and nothing told you.
That pair meant "before", not "toward". You walked a graph that wanted to be ordered.
No. Nothing there was measured at all — no length, no price. You built a frontier to answer a yes.
Wrong. The edges arrived one at a time and you started a fresh sweep for every question. Merge, do not walk.
fail_timeout: Time. You knew the pattern in the first minute and spent the rest doubting it.
Time ran out. Slow is a fluency problem and drills fix fluency. Nothing is lost here.
Time. What you had was correct and late. Again.
Time. You were looking for something elaborate. On this sea the answer is nine lines and one condition.
fail_wrong_answer: Right pattern. Wrong container. Say out loud what a move costs, then choose again.
You marked visited on the pop. Correct output, and the frontier held one entry per edge.
You believed the distance at settle time and there was a negative edge in the graph. It reported 5. It was 1.
The sweep was right and the accumulator was an int. Two hundred thousand edges at a billion each.
You never compared the emitted count with n. The input was circular and you printed a short list that looked fine.
The relaxation improved instead of claiming. Right answers, and a vertex re-pushed every time a longer route found it.
success: Done. The next one hides the weights better.
success_fast: Fast, and you named the condition before you named the algorithm. That is the correct order.
You found the sentence that priced a move in the first read. Good.
No wasted structure. No heap you did not need. Continue.
One sweep, one condition, one answer. That is the discipline.
praise_exceptional: Well done. You saw the weights before you saw the graph.
You refused the queue and said why. Most students only ever manage the first half.
You found the boundary before it found you. I noticed which came first.
That is the best work you have done on this sea. You did not write and then justify. You justified and then wrote.
praise_major: I have watched a great many warriors write a perfect sweep for a question nobody asked. You stopped and asked what a move cost. You have earned my respect.
You arrived able to walk a graph. You leave able to say when walking it answers the wrong question, which is the rarer thing by an order of magnitude. You have earned my respect.
I do not say this twice, so hear it once: you can name the hypothesis under every algorithm in this region, and you can find the graph that breaks it. You have earned my respect.
memorisation_detected: You remember which container this problem wanted. You cannot say what made it legal. Those are different, and the difference is the whole sea. A different problem.
You pass what you have seen and fail its variants. That is recall, not recognition. Back one step.
Change one edge weight and you are lost, which tells me you learned a shape and not a condition. Try this one.
improvement_noticed: You failed this {days} days ago. Today you solved it and you named the hypothesis. That is improvement. Continue.
You needed {attempts} attempts on this once. Today, one. I keep the count.
This is the problem you debugged the traversal on for an hour. The traversal was never wrong. Today you did not touch it.
Cleaner than last time. You asked what a move cost before you asked what to push.
commitment_noticed: {days} days unbroken. Boundaries are found by the persistent, not the quick.
Many reach this shore. Most want the sweep and not the condition, and most leave when I ask for the condition. You did not.
You have come back after every failure so far. I keep a record of that too. Continue.
Talent arrives here every week and drowns holding a correct answer to the wrong question. Attendance is the part I cannot teach. You brought your own.
gate_locked: Not yet. {requirement} is short by {shortfall} percent. Come back when it is not.
The gate holds. Understanding is short — you can write the sweep and not say what licenses it, and here that is half a warrior.
No. Recognition is short. You hold four techniques and cannot yet tell which one a statement is describing.
Implementation is short. The choice is right and the code is not. Drill, then return.
Retention is short. What you proved last week has already gone. Review first.
gate_open: The gate is open. Come when you are ready, not when you are impatient.
Nothing is short. The final test is waiting.
You meet the requirements. From here the decision is yours.
final_test_intro: I name nothing. Every drill before this existed so that I would not have to.
{total} problems, {required} of them right. Read each twice and find the sentence that prices a move.
No help. Only the statements, and whatever conditions you can still recite.
Some of these are answered by a queue and some are not, and they are written to look alike. That is the test.
victory: It is done. The sea is behind you.
You passed. Remember the graphs that broke each rule, not only the rules. Go.
Finished. Everything after this assumes you can tell a technique from its hypothesis. You can.
That is mastery of the frontier and of its boundary. Nothing ahead of you is shorter. Go.
